A DeGroot iteration on a three-group matrix with transient members confirms Theorem 3's per-group normalization, and a Monte Carlo run agrees with the exact formula. Adding a seed already in its target state can halve the chance of exact assembly (38 of 40 significant decreases confirmed with 3000 runs), and island coverage predicts the chance better than the number of seeds. Neither VIC nor ICN transfers: VIC ranks seed sets worse than the monotone island union (Spearman 0.22 against 0.54) and flags 193 additions as harmful of which 2 are. The harmful seeds have large islands; the errors are order effects at the binding threshold. A post hoc predictor, threshold-front forcing (TFF), meets the pre-registered criterion on five fresh architectures (Spearman 0.64 against 0.48, AUC 0.94, recall 0.66, precision 0.11). In numpy (scratch/studies/lead-005/, 15 tests), 300 random 4-state systems driven by a 3-symbol Markov signal through Metropolis kernels satisfy the per-switch identity (Eq. 14), the summed identity (Eq. 17) and the heat identity (Eq. 19) to 3e-15, and the bounds (Eqs. 16, 18, 21) in every instance; no step's nostalgia is negative; Monte Carlo trajectories agree with the exact averages. With the drive made to depend on the system's state (500 systems), the identities and the summed bound still hold, but a step's nostalgia is negative in 405, the summed nostalgia in 323, and the dissipation and the excess work in 6. In an 8-percept loop where the predictive partition is a sticky nuisance and the interventional partition is the context the action must match, the memory that keeps only the context is the cheapest that does the task by every cost measured; the policy that uses it changes its nostalgia from ln 2 to 0 and leaves its heat per step unchanged. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
